passages.text: The card earns 3% on dining, including takeout and eligible delivery. It also earns 3% at drugstores.
Travel booked through Chase Travel earns 5%. All other purchases earn 1.5%.
There is no annual fee.
New accounts get a 0% intro APR on purchases and balance transfers for 15 months from opening.
After the intro period the variable APR is 18.24% to 27.74%. A balance transfer costs $5 or 5% of the amount, whichever is greater.
Each foreign transaction carries a fee of 3% of the amount in US dollars.
Purchase protection covers new items against damage or theft for 120 days, up to $500 per item. Extended warranty adds one year to eligible warranties of three years or less.
Trip cancellation and interruption insurance can pay up to $1,500 per traveler and $6,000 per trip.
Rewards can be redeemed for cash with no minimum and do not expire while the account is open. Using points on Amazon values each point at 0.8 cents.

general.text: A grace period is the time between the end of a billing cycle and the payment due date. Paying the full balance by the due date usually means no interest on purchases. Paying less means interest on the unpaid part.

source.title: What is a grace period for a credit card? (CFPB)

general.text: Card issuers must mail or deliver bills at least 21 days before the payment is due.

source.title: What is a grace period for a credit card? (CFPB)

general.text: APR stands for annual percentage rate. It is the yearly cost of borrowing on a card, and the CFPB says you can avoid interest on purchases by paying the full balance each month by the due date.

source.title: What is a credit card interest rate? What does APR mean? (CFPB)

general.text: Paying more than the minimum each month lowers the total interest paid. It also shortens the time it takes to clear the balance.
A payment counts as late when at least the minimum payment does not arrive by the time and date on the bill.
Federal rules bar a penalty fee larger than the dollar amount tied to the violation. For a late payment, the fee cannot be more than the minimum payment that was due.
Paying on time is the top factor for a strong credit score. The CFPB suggests using no more than 30 percent of total credit limits. Applying for a lot of credit in a short time can worry lenders.

source.title: How do I get and keep a good credit score? (CFPB)

general.text: If a lost or stolen card is reported before anyone uses it, the cardholder owes nothing for unauthorized charges. If it is used first, federal law caps the cardholder's share at $50. If only the card number is stolen, there is generally no liability.

source.title: Am I responsible for unauthorized charges if my credit cards are lost or stolen? (CFPB)

general.text: Under the Fair Credit Billing Act, a written dispute must reach the issuer within 60 days after the first bill with the error was sent. The issuer must acknowledge it within 30 days and resolve it within 90 days. The disputed amount can be withheld during the investigation.

source.title: Using Credit Cards and Disputing Charges (FTC Consumer Advice)

general.text: A secured card works with a cash deposit, such as $500, that sets how much you can spend. Payments are reported to the three major credit bureaus, which helps build a credit history.

source.title: What are some ways to start or rebuild a good credit history? (CFPB)

general.text: An authorized user is someone the account holder asks the issuer to give a card to. Anyone the account holder hands the card or card number to is also treated as an authorized user.
A balance transfer moves debt from one card to another, sometimes for a fee. Promotional low rates on transfers often expire.
An introductory rate must last at least six months unless the cardholder is more than 60 days late. The issuer must say how long it lasts and what rate follows.

source.title: How long can I keep a low rate on a balance transfer or other introductory rate? (CFPB)

general.text: A 0% balance transfer does not shield new purchases. While a balance is carried, new purchases can build interest from the day they are made.

source.title: Do I pay interest on new purchases after I get a zero or low rate balance transfer? (CFPB)

general.text: Issuers must list per purchase transaction fees, such as foreign transaction fees, in the rate and fee table that comes with a card application.

source.title: 12 CFR 1026.60 Credit and charge card applications and solicitations (CFPB)

general.text: Cash advances often carry a flat or percent fee and a higher APR than purchases. Interest starts the day the cash is taken, with no grace period. Many cards set a lower limit for cash advances.

source.title: Can I withdraw money from my credit card at an ATM? (CFPB)
